Michigan Invicta

Act One: Ohio Delenda Est

2045 - the post-Union. A series of populist administrations have leeched the federal bureaucracy dry for purposes both ideological and financial, leaving states as the only effective governing bodies. The pieces of the federal military not already sold for parts have been co-opted to state militias through means both legal and clandestine. The great state of Michigan, already known in some circles as the Frontier Republic, benefits from strong control of the Lakes, good relations with stable Canada, and native heavy manufacturing and high technology. But all is not well. Greedy eyes peer northward, seeking to plunder from Michigan what their own foolishness squandered at home. Ohio withdraws from the Great Lakes Compact and regional trade and defense treaties and marches to war. Adrian, MI is largely undefended and rapidly seized by the 1st Ohio (Buckeyes) (sorry Victor) - but, crucially, is not yet Integrated into Ohioan supply lines (gray icon). This means 1st Ohio cannot resupply or reinforce while they defend the city. The 2nd Ohio (Bobcats) digs in at Toledo, expecting the ancestral grudge to be a battlefield. Force composition of both is unknown, though at least infantry and technicals were reported. 1st Michigan (Wolverines) have mustered at Ann Arbor, while 2nd Michigan (Spartans) are in Jackson, having been sent from Lansing toward the likely front line. Supreme Commander @TribuneAquila𓅰𓅸, the command is tuebor, and all units await your orders.

The Iron Brigade narrowly beats the 1st Ohio to Coldwater, hastily digging in. As the attack comes, technicals fan out and engage the AT Infantry groups, destroying 10 of the 12 but losing all 10 technical groups in return. These are the first Michigan casualties of the war. The Ohio force continues on foot into the city, where a meat grinder awaits. 10 Infantry and 2 AT Infantry groups are defeated decisively by the defending Michigan infantry. Then, seizing the initiative, the defenders' AT Infantry push out and demolish many of the surviving Ohio transport trucks with shoulder-fired unguided rockets. The 3rd Michigan, the Iron Brigade, defends Coldwater with 4 Infantry, 10 AT Infantry, and 10 Transports surviving, and resupplies. The 1st Ohio, now only 17 surviving Transports with no combat capability, routs towards Ohio - unaware of events in Bryan, OH. It is that very city that the 2nd Michigan, Spartans, seize without a fight. It is under Michigan control, but not yet joined to Michigan supply lines - it can be Integrated into supply lines for a cost in Unity next turn. The 4th Michigan, Tigers, speeds towards Defiance, OH, but will not arrive until next turn. A new division is raised in Adrian, the 5th Michigan "Arsenal", named for the Arsenal of Democracy and the Willow Run aircraft plant more specifically. Industrial sabotage has limited its procurement to 7 of each Tech 1 unit, but 4 Bulk Transporter squads provide a large amount of logistics capacity. Reconnaissance of forces stationed in Toledo (there is nothing to recon in cities without forces) reveals the Ohioan defenders have brought in more AT Infantry to defend against FPV drones, and the first unit of high-altitude loitering suicide drones from Arsenal-1 which Michigan AT Infantry will not be able to defend against. Their range is superior to FPV drones and their onboard explosive payload is extremely powerful, but they are not yet accurate.

Their namesake the 127th Fighter Squadron that once stood at Selfridge, they now fly ten flights of Aerotechnicals - converted civilian Cessna 172s, Piper Cubs, and other light aircraft pressed into service to drop gravity bombs and fire unguided rockets in much the same way as civilian pickup trucks became Technicals. The masses of infantry garrisoning Lorain are unceremoniously wiped out, and the Tigers are at last able to advance into the city. After months of bombardment, then later intense urban fighting, command has made the decision to go all in on the capture of Cleveland. The Wolverines make one final barrage as 20 dedicated Breacher Teams and 30 Infantry sections from the Tigers push north from Parma into Cleveland proper. Fighting is brutal, house by house, and the Ohioan machine gun nests prove deadly. The Breachers are well trained and well equipped for urban combat, however, and methodically eliminate pockets of resistance block by block. With regular Infantry supporting, the suicidal assault becomes merely very deadly - the Ohioans lose 6 MG Teams, 10 AT Infantry, and all 59 Partisan groups, while the Tigers lose 15 Breacher Teams, 20 Infantry, and all 30 of their Transports (owing to the Partisans' ability). Cleveland, at last, is in Michigander hands. 70 Logistics and 4 Tunnel-Bunkers owned by Ohio were destroyed in the course of the fighting. Ohio gains 2 levels of Escalation and is now Escalation 12. The Yellowjackets return to Toledo to pivot towards operations in the Columbus region, while trouble brews to the south. Arsenal pushes south and captures Greenville, but uncovers Ohio's newest regiment, the Musketeers (8th OH). This is quite a large force seemingly looking to roll up the western flank, with 30 Drones, 15 MG Teams, and 15 AT Infantry. It does not yet attack Arsenal, owing to the Laser Defenders' excellent defense against drones, but battle is imminent. The Spartans sit immobile, again robbed of industrial capacity for new Transports by the needs of the Cleveland front. Intelligence reports attached. War Plan Blue is in effect.

Momentum begins to swing, and the war is in peril. Arsenal (5th MI) is reinforced with 10 units of brand new IFVs and 5 Bulk Transporters at Greenville. Their armor, manufactured in Warren and Sterling Heights where ex-General Dynamics Land Systems assets were nationalized into the Michigan State Armory, is resistant to anything in the Ohioan arsenal save a direct strike from a Loitering Munition, and their 20mm autocannons can dish out a staggering amount of damage. The rest of the 5th Michigan, however, remains vulnerable, and the Ohioans move to exploit this. The Musketeers (8th OH) depart north towards Lima, but as they do they launch a staggering 54 units of FPV Drones against Arsenal. The 5th Michigan's seven units of Laser Defenders -the most of any division- down a staggering 28 of them, and AT Infantry nail 4 more, but 22 units of Drones survive to strike the defenders at Greenville. They preferentially strike logistics, taking out 21 of 22 Transports and 1 of 5 Bulk Transporters. Arsenal is now effectively stranded in Greenville, unable to move to counter the Musketeers. Then, it gets worse. A group of militia crosses the Indiana-Ohio border at Bluffton, claiming to be Ohioan military. Intelligence suggests they are Rivermen, Hoosier (Indianan) paramilitaries trained in Indiana but staffed by Ohioans. They seize Van Wert. With the Musketeers blocking the road to Lima, Greenville (and the 5th Michigan) is now Interdicted and cut off from resupply. Then, it gets worse. The Knight of Columbus fire a staggering 25 units of Loitering Munitions at the Spartans, having clearly built up units from the Arsenal-1 drone megafactory in Cleveland. 11 fail to make the target, but 14 hit. The Spartans' Laser Defenders down another 10, and the remaining 4 wings all hit. All 4 Operators, 7 Infantry, 2 AT Infantry, and 5 Laser Defenders of the 2nd Michigan "Spartans" are lost at Marion, along with 45 Logistics. The southern front has collapsed.

The F-16M Graywolf, an (admittedly unauthorized) variant of the venerable F-16 Fighting Falcon substituting locally-made parts and trimmed down complexity, is issued both to the 6th Michigan "Yellowjackets" and a new 7th Michigan "Red Devils", 5 units to each. In Dayton, southeast of 5th MI (Arsenal), a new Ohioan unit is raised - the 9th Ohio "Dragons". It is not yet combat effective, but may in time attempt to collapse the pocket at Greenville. Artillery and air attacks on Columbus continue apace, leveling another 46 of the remaining 70 Tunnel-Bunkers. Months earlier, around the same time as Michigan's air wings were facing off against Ohio-commanded F-15EXs in the skies over Cincinatti, an entirely covert, but no less important, battle was being waged. As the Tigers seize Portsmouth and push towards Peebles, they pass through the town of Piketon, OH, not even large enough to warrant an entry on the theater map. In this town sits an ex-DoE facility, the American Centrifuge Plant, a uranium enrichment facility for commercial reactors. Since the start of the war, this plant has been operated under Ohioan control and enriching uranium far above the criticality required for fission plants. This operation is kept top secret, with runners sending instructions and reports directly between Ohioan leadership in Columbus and plant leadership lest the Michiganders infiltrate their digital communications. Workers are sequestered in on-base housing, disconnected from the internet, many of them formally marked as refugees or MIA by the Ohioan government to cover their tracks. The deception works. Michigan's intelligence services are in their infancy, led by ex-Federal veterans but lacking institutional knowledge and human assets. When the Tigers capture the American Centrifuge Plant, the intelligence agents that arrive in their wake find no reason to question the falsified documents and on-site stores that imply the facility was shuttered with the outbreak of war. In reality, its highly enriched uranium and skilled workers were shuttled north to Columbus, posing as refugees, barely evading the Tigers' advance and sentries in the salient. Once safely underground in the city, assembly of the 100 kiloton fission bomb started - The Buckeye, Ohio's ace in the hole. Ohioan leadership considered using it to force a peace deal, but now with Michigan air power and special forces so dominant, they could not take the risk.
10:29 PM
Instead, as the situation looks dire for Columbus, The Buckeye is loaded into a truck and driven up the humanitarian corridor along OH-16. Guarded by the most die hard of the Ohioan military in plainclothes with concealed rifles and MGs, the miniature convoy gets as close as they can to Horns Hill Park, elevation 1087 feet, the highest point in Newark and the natural location for the Wolverines' artillery batteries. They cannot approach closer Mt. Vernon Road nearly a mile distant, but that is more than close enough. The Buckeye is armed, and the team evacuates while a handful of fanatics volunteer to stay until the end. The Buckeye detonates. Nearly the entire city of Newark is consumed by the fireball, and windows are broken in neighboring towns. 11,600 residents die in moments, another 2,700 passing refugees with them. Over the coming weeks, 17,800 of the survivors will succumb to Acute Radiation Syndrome or to their injuries. With over 32,000 civilians dead, the atomic bombing of Newark reaches nearly half of the death toll of Nagasaki. The Buckeye does have its intended military effect. Of the forces at Newark, 45 units of Laser Defenders, 27 units of artillery, 16 units of Transports, 11 units of Bulk Transporters, 8 units of IFVs, and 2 Command Teams are killed outright. All stockpiled Logistics not outright destroyed are tainted by radiation. The survivors of the Wolverines and Arsenal rout south. They are heavily radiation poisoned and most of the survivors will not survive the week even with medical care. Both units will be effectively destroyed next turn.
10:30 PM
Newark, Coshocton, New Philadelphia, Massillon, and Canton form the extent of the plume of radioactive fallout drifting northeast on the wind. Evacuations of these cities and towns begin immediately, but it is not known when it will be safe to return. The carnage does not stop there. Columbus spies the nuclear fireball and makes its move, launching 40 units of Drones at the Tigers and Lions. A mere 6 Drones completely destroy the undermanned Tigers which had depended on Arsenal's air defense shield, and 20 Drones wear down the Lions' few Laser Defenders - allowing another 11 to slip through and finish off the unit. The 4th Michigan "Tigers" and the 8th Michigan "Lions" have been destroyed. Now the counterattack can begin in earnest. A unit of Transports and Technicals departs Columbus and recaptures the now-undefended Lancaster. It is clear that they seek to reconnect their lines to West Virginia and reestablish Federal aid. Another unit of Technicals and Transports pushes west, threatening Dayton and its air power with bombardment on the ground with drones next turn. If they can destroy the Graywolves of Six Pack or force them to leave, Michigan will lose its air power projection over southern Ohio. War Plan Blue is insufficient for this contingency. Kanzokax𓅊 12/25/2025 12:15 AM

The Fall of Columbus

Christmas Eve, 2047

ATTN: @everyone

Columbus' once-proud skyline has turned burned out and haggard, skyscrapers condemned or collapsed amidst the constant bombardment by shell and by air. Industrial and business sites have been struck so many times that wartime production has in some cases been restarted on the sixth or seventh set of ruins of the industrial targets bombed before. Arsenal-1, the colossal drone factory in which Ohioan leadership had placed so much hope, lies shattered. In the last few holdouts around the Command bunkers of Ohioan leadership, 220 units of Partisans, many undermanned and starving, hold out against the tide. Michigan Intelligence has improved considerably, and these pockets are destroyed by fragmentation shells from the Mason railguns as they are spotted by HUMINT, SIGINT, or as the Red Arrows move cautiously cross the Scioto River into the downtown and brewing districts. 200 Partisans are felled, leaving only 20 around the cluster of Ohioan leadership that Michigan hopes to capture alive. Rather than risk killing these criminals by air strike, the Red Arrows move in with fresh Bulk Transporter support. Their 20mm autocannons make short work of the diehard defenders, and by 7:40pm on December 24th, Operators attached to the Red Arrows have breached the command staff bunkers. By 10:51pm, the last of them emerge with the leadership -both alive and dead- of the state of Ohio.
12:15 AM
With the news of Columbus' capture and the last Ohioan leaders' arrests, the little remaining resistance in the city and in southern Ohio collapses. Michigan forces oversee the surrender of the remaining Ohio militias and regulars. The eyes of the world are on Michigan, the first state to be attacked by a fellow state following the federal collapse - and not only to repulse that attack, but to go on tbe offensive, to neutralize the foe, and ultimately overcome a nuclear attack as a state government turned into a national one.
12:16 AM
The Buckeye affair remains universally condemned, and Ohioan leadership is held to account both inside the fragmented states and internationally. Michigan tries some leaders themselves, others it hands over to federal judges it trusts, and a few even go to the Hague for a formal war crimes tribunal. Most are imprisoned, some for life, and some are executed. It is clear that the Ohioan upper leadership had aspirations of nationhood, with the ex-Federal backers to make it a reality. Michigan Intelligence puts a priority on uncovering the power brokers that allowed the expertise and equipment to build a homegrown nuclear weapon to end up in Ohio's hands.
12:16 AM
With the entirety of Ohio in Michigan hands, the world waits to see how the first American state to overcome another will handle the aftermath of this unique war. Michigan leadership has no appetite for an insurgency, nor for another war in ten or twenty years, and so puts the colossal industrial and logistical powerhouse it had built for the war effort to work: first in feeding and housing refugees, then in rebuilding critical infrastructure and ultimately the economy of Ohio as a fully integrated part of Michigan. Timetables are set for elections, but it is clear to all that Ohio will be in reconstruction for a long time before then. Michigan hopes to learn from the countless lessons of conquerors who failed to integrate their holdings and give the former Ohioans safety, security, and employment so that they will be too bought in to indulge in nationalist fervor. Despite setbacks, ambushes, and a tenacious enemy, War Plan Blue was, ultimately, a success. For the first time in a very long time, the guns of Michigan fall silent. And the snow begins to fall.

Act Two: Live Free or Die

December, 2055. The federal collapse has been felt in every corner of the formerly United States. Not all states possessed strong state-level governments unmarred by partisan bickering, and many of these still squabble over which warlord to put in the Oval Office, or at Cheyenne Mountain, or at a number of other sites holy to the American coronation mythos. On the Eastern Seaboard, the power players are Canada, New York, and Virginia, the latter coming into a possession of a massive quantity of ex-Federal military and intelligence assets, and large swaths of the civil service suddenly looking for gainful employment. Virginia found a useful ally in the reborn Commonwealth of New England in much the same way as Canada found in Michigan, a helpful buffer against more belligerent states and a proxy with which to foil their plans in a plausibly deniable fashion. The Commonwealth is neither the richest nor the most populous player on the Eastern Seaboard, nor is it possessed of the police or paramilitary structures upon which a suitable military could be constructed. It does, however, possess the most enduring sites and symbols of the American Revoluton, ideals not easily discarded even in a fractured union - Lexington and Concord, Paul Revere, the Boston Tea Party. With Virginia's backing, training, and technical assistance, New England possesses the mythos to attract young men and women who yearn for the past and molds them into the first units of a passable fighting force.
8:53 PM
This is soon revealed to be prudent. After a series of border actions by New York-aligned paramilitaries prove fruitless and the appetite in Canada for military adventurism south of the border is tempered by political scandal, the two turn to the European Union as a means of pacifying their disagreeable, rapidly rearming neighbor. The timing is fortuitous - European leadership is desperate to catch the falling mantle of American hegemony, as much for global economic stability as for their own security, and there are no tougher opponents to prove themselves against than the Americans, the land with a gun behind every blade of grass. If the EU can keep the peace in New England, it can keep the peace anywhere - and no one, from Russia to China to India, would consider upending the Western world order. Conflict would also distract populations of many of the largest European nations from their own crippling internal strife. A consensus rapidly forms. New York and Canada demand the dismantling of the Commonwealth's military and economic concessions for good measure. The Commonwealth of New England refuses - it will not give up its political or economic independence. After considerable backroom negotiations with the Europeans, during which the two aggressors agree to pay the costs of the expedition, the European Union agrees to enforce the disarmament of the Commonwealth. Against the arrayed expeditionary forces of over a dozen nations, surely New England will back down and accept her fate rather than risk bloody war.
8:53 PM
They do not. Even as aircraft carriers and amphibious landing ships like the Queen Elizabeth and Juan Carlos anchor miles off the coast of Boston, the nascent Commonwealth military prepares for the worst. Calls for surrender are repeated across official and social channels, but they do not have the intended demoralizing effect. The citizens of the Commonwealth turn from fear to anger: first at New York and Canada's attempt to divvy up their land and their wealth, and now at this attempt at intimidation. The Europeans are fully committed now, and backing down would mean a catastrophic loss of face - it could mean an invasion of Taiwan, or fighting in the Baltics, and almost certainly an economic crash to boot. For the stability of the Western world, they must make good on their threats. The first battlegroup makes landfall nearly unopposed at Portland, and pushes north towards the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard. Another force turns south towards Boston. The refrain from air power is intentional - the Europeans are still calling for surrender, and want to avoid pitched battle and the optics of civilian casualties if they can. This may be a fatal mistake. Commonwealth forces muster defensively at Kittery and Biddeford, hoping to stall the European advance and buy time to negotiate heavier armament from Virginia and broader mobilization from New England and the sympathetic abroad. The new Minutemen think to their ancestors who mustered to resist European invasion on these very lands centuries ago, and it fills them with grim determination. The Commonwealth will not fall. @SupremeAllyCommander ass biscuit - the forces of the Commonwealth of New England are ready for your order. The Commonwealth cannot fall. Not now - not ever.

Kanzokax𓅊 12/30/2025 11:02 PM
The European forces advance down roads that have not seen foreign invaders in centuries, eyes of the world upon them. 2nd Battlegroup, "Clubs" for this operation, push south into Biddeford, ME, and it is here that the Battle of Biddeford will mark the first combat of the war. An armor-heavy formation of 20 German Leopard MBTs, 10 Spanish VAMTAC personnel carriers, and 10 Unmanned Combat Ground Vehicles (colloqually "ug-vees", both a loose acronym and portmanteau of "ugly" and "humvee") carry 10 Infantry and 5 Medic units into the city. The ugvees push in first to draw defenders' fire and to give the armor time to penetrate the city. All 10 units of UCGVs are destroyed on contact with the Commonwealth military, but they give as good as they get with their 20mm autocannons and 30 Gun Trucks (much the same as the Technicals out west, many of them GMC Sierras, though F-150s are not at all uncommon) are destroyed in the opening maneuver warfare. This is a checkmark for drone warfare, but the battle has only just begun. Knowing full well the Commonwealth does not yet have passable anti-armor, Gun Trucks and Infantry are ordered to focus fire on the VAMTACs and their Infantry. All 10 VAMTACs are destroyed, but they take down 30 Minutemen with them. While all 10 EU Infantry and 5 Medics are killed, the Medic ability saves 5 Inf. The EU force has been whittled down to armor, and the situation warrants the local commander to throw Brussels' angry micromanaging to the wind and unleash the armored fist. 120mm shells and coaxial machine gun rounds fly, decimating the defenders - the remaining 30 Gun Trucks are engaged and destroyed with HEAT rounds and 7.62mm MG rounds. All 20 professional Infantry are also flushed from their fortifications and cut down - but, in a small mercy for New England, their deaths buy time for 30 Minutemen and 20 valuable Drones to escape, neither of which can pierce tank armor. The 1st Commonwealth "Patriots" routs inland. (edited)

Further south, the 2nd Commonwealth "Continentals" have heard snippets from the Battle of Biddeford just north of them and local commanders quickly discuss how to better resist the second force (1st EUBG, "Spades") closing in on the Portsmouth Naval Yards. FPV Drones let fly as soon as they sight the European ugvees, and drone-on-drone violence marks the opening of the Battle of the Yard. All 10 UGV units are destroyed at range, and this creates more breathing room for the Gun Trucks to do their work. As the VAMTACs advance, the scavenged and purchased mounted MGs chatter, knocking out each of the personnel carriers and killing the Infantry and Medics inside. The VAMTACs and dismounting infantry inflict 30 losses on the Gun Trucks before they die. As before, 5 EU Infantry survive thanks to medical intervention. The retaliation of the Leopards is immediate, knocking out the remaining 30 Gun Trucks and all 40 professional Infantry. Incredibly, the Commonwealth has held on to the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard by a thread. While they cannot fight main battle tanks, nor can the Leopards seize the site without infantry support. Minutemen dig in while European commanders regroup and request more Infantry to take the facility proper. (edited)

The air war has begun. Shocked at the tenacity of the defenders, who were supposed to fold and rout when faced with modern military power, Brussels has authorized air strikes and helicopter insertions to speed the operation along. The world watches, and Europe's fortunes ride on this war. From aircraft carriers in the Gulf of Maine, 20 units of Eurofighter Ultimas and their Loyal Wingman drone attendants launch and pound the defenders at Portsmouth with precision munitions. Conducting air strikes inside the complex is exceedingly tricky, as the Euros would also prefer to keep the facility intact. The airstikes destroy 5 Gun Trucks and 4 Mechanized Recons, and wipe out much of the remaining defenders - all 72 entrenched Infantry, and 14 Minutemen. During the strike, the New England men unleash a surprise of their own - a cache of 6 Stingers, which down 4 units of Eurofighters and damage another so severely that they must ditch over the Gulf of Maine. With 5 Eurofighters down, the Euro's hand has been decisively slapped. A further 12 Minutemen are called away for reasons which will be apparent shortly, but the remaining 34 defenders will be sufficient to use the Javelins provided to them. The Leopards roll in to finish the job - and are greeted by the second cache of 18 Javelins. These the Minutemen use to inflict 12 kills on the Leopards, and oily smoke from the tank deaths billows into the overcast sky. The 17 surviving tank units have their revenge, however, and obliterate the defenders. The Euros have Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, but they can't Integrate or use it without Infantry. To this end, the naval group flies out 10 Merlin helicopter units carrying 15 Infantry and 5 SAS Teams. It is here that the final trap is sprung: with the 1st Commonwealth firmly in drone launch range, they launch all 25 Drones as the landed Infantry are taking stock of their new prize. All 15 Infantry and 5 SAS Teams are killed. Portsmouth Naval Shipyard remains firmly contested.
12:00 AM
At the same time, the European commanders have decided to use their newly authorized air power to do what they wanted to do in the first place before being overruled by bureaucrats: land infantry by helicopter around Boston, quickly decapitating the city. Another 15 Merlins loaded with 24 Infantry and 3 UGVs take off from aircraft carriers and amphibious assault ships and head towards downtown Boston. Minutemen informed by OSINT accounts and distant handlers with access to more conventional military sensors mobilize around Boston, distributing the cache of Stingers placed there earlier. As repurposed severe weather sirens ring out an air raid, Minutemen fire missiles at the approaching Merlins. 12 of the 15 Merlins are downed across the city, raining down trails of black smoke onto the skyline. The remaining 3 land at their pre-sighted targets and drop off their Infantry and UGVs, rapidly making for the safety of the naval group. 4 EU Infantry and 1 UGV unit are an even match for the 12 Minutemen units in the city, and after intense fighting all EU forces are wiped out and only 1 of the 12 Minuteman units remains. Boston is held, but only by the faintest grasp. Ready for orders.

Following the embarrassment of the air assault in Boston, European leadership needs some sort of win to control the media narrative beginning to form. They elect for an airstrike on the 1st Commonwealth "Patriots" who, after launching a massive drone attack to keep Portsmouth contested, now consist only of 40 undefended Transports. 10 Eurofighters are sufficient for the job, and with no Stinger caches anywhere nearby, the result is a turkey shoot. The footage of the overwhelming majority of New England's military transport capacity as burning, twisted wreckage strewn across the 109 near I-95 is a potent and demoralizing image, even if the loss to actual military capacity is manageable. As this happens, the naval group readies another 10 Infantry, 5 Medics, and 5 SAS Teams composing 3rd Battlegroup and flies them out on Merlins to Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, formally capturing it. Intelligence services direct the SAS teams to begin packing and scanning initial documents and items of value ahead of a more formal takeover. The Yard has fallen. A 4th Battlegroup lands at Portland the slow way via LCVP landing craft, freeing the helos for more important jobs. This is composed of 10 UCGVs, 10 VAMTACs, 12 EU Infantry, and 8 Medics. 4th EUBG intends to push up through Maine, closing off any threat to Canada and tempting the Commonwealth into wasting personnel in the north. Now is the Commonwealth's time to strike. At Manchester, 15 units of Loitering Munitions fresh from the factory are placed on launch rails. To the east, 1st Battlegroup's Leopard tanks have just been stopped by detected IEDs, and their attendants are carefully disarming or detonating them. Unchallenged on the ground, the heavy armor presents a nice column to target. All Munitions launch, and 9 reach the target. The European 4th Battlegroup moves north and seizes Brunswick and Lewiston. Augusta is now threatened by the European advance, and Mainers demand action from the Commonwealth. In the North Atlantic, another 2 units of Eurofighter Ultimas make their way to the naval group as direly needed reinforcements. At the Portsmouth Naval Yards, the mauled Leopards of 1st Battlegroup merge with the defensive Infantry force of 3rd EUBG, licking their wounds. In their place, their comrades in 2nd Battlegroup "Spades" drive hard and seize Concord, which is undefended. The symbolism of this moment is anything but subtle. Unlike in the Revolution, there will be no Minutemen rushing to defend Concord - they are spread too thin, and Boston is too dear a prize. 2nd EUBG receives 4 units of airlifted UCGVs from the naval group, the best that can be done to provide some anti-infantry power and ablative armor of sorts on short notice. Finally, the bulk of the Merlins' airlift capacity goes towards a landing at Race Point, where 5th Battlegroup takes Provincetown, composed of a variety of VAMTACs, UCGVs, Infantry, Medics, and SAS. It is clear that if the Euros cannot have Boston by air or by land via I-95 then they will come get it by sea - specifically, pushing up and around Cape Cod which is currently largely undefended. In Lynn, Eurofighters launch airstrikes on the large Minuteman training encampments and caches, hoping to score easy kills and cut out of the heart of this mobile militia force that has plagued them thus far. To their misfortune, command has the resources to scatter the Minutemen out before the first bombs drop - with the exception of those required to man the cache of Stinger missiles at Lynn. 4 Minutemen give their lives to shoot down 3 Eurofighter Ultimas - a good price for their lives by any standard. The EU remains vexed by New England's guerilla warfare.

Inside Canadian territory, a civilian semi truck takes Route 2 deep into New Brunswick. It is the culmination of a long and arduous road walked by hundreds in total secrecy, stretching back over a decade. At the close of the Ohio War, the nascent Commonwealth was one of several groups who approached Ohioan nuclear physicists, uranium enrichment staff, and intelligence officers and offered them a new identity and new life in exchange for their expertise. Given the alternative of a war crimes tribunal and execution, few refused. The intelligence services of Michigan and the Commonwealth actually sparred in the months after the war, the Wolverines eager to find the scientists responsible for the Buckeye and the New Englanders eager to obtain their knowledge. Ultimately, enough of them had been exfiltrated to New England for research to begin. The project was codenamed Plymouth Rock, and before long, the device that took shape was simply known as The Rock. It had begun as an outlandish contingency plan, and then when the Europeans had come knocking with their "peacekeeping" operation it was seen as a liability because it could not be feasibly used against them. The Europeans had known about Plymouth Rock, of course. It was one of the reasons they were so eager to seize Boston rapidly by air insertion, to scour the city for its materials and labs. But the Commonwealth had been nimble, relocating assets as the battlegroups threatened them. The Canadians no doubt knew as well, but after dozens of false leads, EUCA command had become convinced that the project had stalled out.
11:57 PM
They were about to pay for that assumption. In an act of sheer audacity, the Rock would be inserted exactly the same way the Buckeye was ten years ago - in a semi truck staffed by armed plainclothes fanatics who would die with the bomb, who would drive it to a military target right against a civilian highway. It was so foolish, in fact, that Canadian intelligence had discounted it as an attack vector. Radiological detectors were only in use at a handful of places, mostly border weigh stations. The semi containing The Rock was snuck onto the Canadian side and to its target without any suspicion. CFB Gagetown is a colossal base, but the primary target lay directly off of Route 2, next to the town of Oromocto. The semi pulled off onto an access road near the fence, not even needing to risk the payload in a gate rush. The men inside were beginning to exchange their farewells when their leader triggered the device, to complete the mission before the fear of death caused any operational problems. The Rock did its job flawlessly. A 100 kiloton device modeled after the Buckeye, its detonation immediately destroyed a huge portion of the 4,280 stockpiled Logistics there. Fallout contaminates the rest, immediately depriving the Canadian war machine of over 90% of the fuel, food, ammunition, and parts they need to continue their advance. The town of Oromocto is flattened, and 3,000 of the city's 9,000 residents are killed instantly. Another 3,600 would succumb to Acute Radiation Syndrome in the weeks and months ahead, as well as thousands of Canadian military personnel. The entirety of the 5/5th Mechanized receives Radiation Poisoning 4. From there, the fallout plume spreads northeast, clear out to the sea. Sussex, Salisbury, and Moncton are evacuated. The world stops and watches in awe and horror as another nuclear weapon is detonated in North America - but this time, as a weapon of self-defense. In Ottawa, heads will roll.
